inhibitor_layers.name: cyan
inhibitor_layers.label: estimate
inhibitor_layers.source: Fujifilm Professional Data Guide AF3-207U (2005), PDF page 31, FUJICOLOR SUPERIA REALA [CS]: https://asset.fujifilm.com/www/us/files/2020-03/3ab271f46f8d71c7e4c91bcedb7de050/ProfessionalFilmDataGuide.pdf -- curve: log_sensitivity_cyan_layer.csv
inhibitor_layers.notes: Fujifilm 4th colour layer: cyan-sensitive, forms no image dye, releases DIR inhibitor into the red-sensitive layer. log_sensitivity is normalised to raw exposure 1 at 18.4 % grey under the reference illuminant; values outside the printed range are a smooth extrapolation. The runtime models the developed silver of this layer with the red layer's characteristic-curve shape.
inhibitor_layers.amount_basis: Estimate, not measured: the data sheet gives the layer's spectral sensitivity but not how strongly it inhibits. The runtime lowers red log exposure by amount * [D(log E_cyan) - D(log E_green)] (departure from neutral; D = red characteristic curve shape). amount_default is the value for which the effective red spectral sensitivity of the full film model (narrowband sweep on mid-grey through spektrafilm.model.develop, default negative DIR-coupler matrix) has a negative lobe at 500-530 nm as deep, relative to its positive peak, as the CIE 1931 r-bar colour-matching function (0.0936 / 0.3476 = 0.269, minimum at 515 nm). Fujifilm describes the 4th layer as giving film the negative red response of human vision around 500-520 nm. The generic DIR couplers alone already give a shallower lobe (effective_red_lobe_ratio_without_layer).
